title: JEE Main 2026 (April 4th, Shift 1) - Mathematics - Binomial Theorem
subject: Mathematics

questions.q: Let the smallest value of $k \in \mathbb{N}$, for which the coefficient of $x^3$ in $(1 + x)^3 + (1 + x)^4 + (1 + x)^5 + \dots + (1 + x)^{99} + (1 + kx)^{100}$, $x \neq 0$, is $\left(43n + \frac{101}{4}\right) \binom{100}{3}$ for some $n \in \mathbb{N}$, be $p$. Then the value of $p + n$ is:
questions.explain:
The given expression is $S = \sum_{r=3}^{99} (1 + x)^r + (1 + kx)^{100}$.
The coefficient of $x^3$ in $\sum_{r=3}^{99} (1 + x)^r$ is $\sum_{r=3}^{99} \binom{r}{3} = \binom{100}{4}$.
The coefficient of $x^3$ in $(1 + kx)^{100}$ is $\binom{100}{3} k^3$.
Total coefficient $= \binom{100}{4} + k^3 \binom{100}{3}$.
Using the property $\binom{n}{r} = \frac{n-r+1}{r} \binom{n}{r-1}$, we have $\binom{100}{4} = \frac{97}{4} \binom{100}{3}$.
Total coefficient $= \left(\frac{97}{4} + k^3\right) \binom{100}{3}$.
Equating this with $\left(43n + \frac{101}{4}\right) \binom{100}{3}$, we get:
$k^3 - 43n = \frac{101 - 97}{4} = 1 \implies k^3 = 43n + 1$.
This implies $k^3 \equiv 1 \pmod{43}$, which can be factored as $(k - 1)(k^2 + k + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{43}$.
Since $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $k$ cannot be $1$ because it would make $n=0$. We solve $k^2 + k + 1 \equiv 0 \pmod{43}$.
$k^2 + k - 42 \equiv 0 \pmod{43} \implies (k + 7)(k - 6) \equiv 0 \pmod{43}$.
The smallest $k \in \mathbb{N}$ satisfying this is $k = 6$.
Substituting $k = 6$ to find $n$: $6^3 = 43n + 1 \implies 216 = 43n + 1 \implies n = 5$.
Therefore, $p = 6$ and $p + n = 6 + 5 = 11$.
